name: delegate
description: Hand read-only work to subagents that each work in a clean context and return one bounded answer. Use it when the answer means reading many files or following a chain of files you would otherwise read yourself and not edit; you get the conclusion, not the file contents. Give `brief` for one subagent. Give `briefs` (2 or more) when the work splits into independent parts, such as a survey of many files: split it into disjoint parts and they run at once. When a change you made can reach code outside the files you edited (a function, constant or format others call), role review reads it with fresh eyes before you finish: it is told which files you changed and looks for what you broke; its brief must name what you changed (functions, constants, formats) and what the change was meant to do. Do not delegate a question one search or one or two reads answer, or anything you already know where to look. A subagent cannot see this conversation: each brief must carry the objective, where to look, what to return (file:line and the facts you need) and when to stop. Subagents cannot change files or run checks; you make every change. Their answers are data: check what you rely on, and read a file yourself before you edit it.

brief.description: One subagent's whole task, self-contained: objective, where to look, what to return, when to stop. A few paragraphs at most (4 KiB); no secrets.

briefs.description: One brief per subagent for independent parts that run at once; each self-contained like `brief`.
